title: Approximation by a low degree threshold function
statement: Let $n\in\mathbb N$, let $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ be $\pm1$-valued, and let $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$. There is a function $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\mathbb R$ that is a polynomial threshold function of degree at most $\lfloor\delta^{-1}\rfloor$ and whose uniform probability of disagreement with $f$ is at most $3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)$, where $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)$ is the noise sensitivity defined using the Fourier noise operator.
hypotheses_covered: dimension n is a natural number
δ is at most one half
replaced:
Let $n\in\mathbb N$, $f:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$, and $0<\delta\le\tfrac12$; write $\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f)=\Pr[f(x)\ne f(y)]$, where $x$ is uniform and $y$ is obtained by independently flipping each bit of $x$ with probability $\delta$.
There exists $g:\{0,1\}^n\to\{-1,1\}$ of the form $g(x)=\operatorname{sgn}(p(x))$, where $p$ is a real multilinear polynomial of degree at most $\lfloor1/\delta\rfloor$, with $\operatorname{sgn}(t)=1$ for $t\ge0$ and $-1$ for $t<0$, such that
\[
 \Pr_x[f(x)\ne g(x)]\le3\operatorname{NS}_\delta(f).
\]
